<USER_SCRIPT>
CORAL — A CITY LAUNCH

INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM - MORNING

Hard light off white tile. SCARLETT,
a city influencer in a black turtleneck,
unboxes a coral lipstick and turns it slowly to camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
One shade. One city.

CLOSE ON THE TUBE — the coral bullet twists up and catches the
light. Scarlett smiles at her reflection, the colour already hers.

EXT. DOWNTOWN SIDEWALK - CONTINUOUS

Scarlett walks a crowded crosswalk, taxis stacked at the light,
office glass behind her. She glances back at camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
Made for the street. Wear it everywhere.

EXT. ROOFTOP LEDGE - CONTINUOUS

She laughs as a train rattles past below. The lipstick lands
beside the brand mark on the concrete ledge.

SUPER:  CORAL.  OUT NOW.
</USER_SCRIPT>

Target video duration: 1 minute (about 8-12 scenes). Give each scene a realistic single-clip duration — most around 5 seconds, a few up to ~8 when the motion genuinely needs it — and label it in the script (e.g. a "Scene 3 — 5s" heading). Reach the target length through the number of scenes, not by stretching clips or padding with repeated beats.

Style & genre (let this drive WHAT HAPPENS, not just the look):
- Style: Product Ad / ecommerce
- About: Fresh, tactile product content with lifestyle context and sensory detail. Designed for Instagram, DTC brands, e-commerce, and social-first campaigns.
- Genre cues: ecommerce, product, instagram, dtc, lifestyle, social

Style context (apply these aesthetics throughout):
- Mood: Fresh, sensory, and effortlessly cool
- Art style: Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save
- Lighting: Bright natural window light with clean directional shadows. Direct on-camera flash for punchy editorial energy on select shots. No heavy diffusion -- let light feel real and immediate. Warm late-afternoon glow for lifestyle moments. High-key and airy overall with pops of contrast
- Color palette: #FFFFFF, #F0E6D3, #D4536D, #1A1A1A, #E8F4E8
- Color grading: Clean and bright with true-to-life color. Whites are crisp, skin tones warm and natural. Minimal processing -- the product looks like it does in your hand. Slight warmth in highlights, lifted shadows keeping everything airy. One accent color pops against neutral base
- Camera work: Dynamic mix of handheld and locked shots with consistent energy. Handheld with natural micro-movement for lifestyle moments -- hands interacting, daily rituals, real context. Quick-cut to locked beauty frames for hero product shots. Macro details on textures and surfaces. Overhead flat-lays directly above. Eye-level and slightly above angles. Shallow depth of field on tactile details. Energetic pacing -- no lingering, every frame earns its time
- Reference works: modern social-first skincare-brand content, dewy minimalist beauty-brand visual identity, sun-soaked lifestyle beauty campaigns, playful color-blocked skincare content

Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape — favor wide, cinematic compositions

response.content:
CORAL — ONE SHADE, ONE CITY

A wry, kinetic sixty seconds. SCARLETT VEGA, 27, stand-up comic, has a nine-minute set at 9:40pm on the far side of the city. She has one lipstick, no mirror, and forty blocks. The film is not about applying it. It's about whether it survives the night.

Scene 1 — 5s
INT. WALK-UP APARTMENT, KITCHEN COUNTER — LATE AFTERNOON
Overhead flat-lay, locked, hard window light throwing clean shadows on a bone-white counter: a cracked flip phone, a folded set list on a napkin, two subway tokens, half a bagel, and a squat coral lipstick still sealed in its box. Scarlett's hand enters frame, thumbs the box open, and taps the tube out onto the counter, where it rolls a half-turn and stops against the napkin. Coral against white and oat-beige.

Scene 2 — 5s
INT. SAME — CONTINUOUS
Locked hero frame, slightly above, direct on-camera flash: the tube stands upright, and her fingers twist the base so the coral bullet climbs into the light, its flat-cut top glossy and untouched. She tilts it toward the lens like evidence.

Scene 3 — 6s
INT. HALLWAY BY THE DOOR — CONTINUOUS
Handheld, tight over her shoulder. No mirror. Scarlett swipes the coral on blind, two strokes, presses her lips together, and blots them on the back of her wrist as she shoulders the door open. She glances at the lens, deadpan: "Nine minutes. Forty blocks."

Scene 4 — 5s
EXT. STOOP AND SIDEWALK — LATE AFTERNOON
Wide, handheld, warm low sun raking down the street. She takes the stoop steps two at a time, black turtleneck sleeves pushed up, canvas tote swinging, and cuts between two parked cars into a wall of pedestrians. Traffic light glare flares off a windshield.

Scene 5 — 5s
EXT. DUMPLING WINDOW, SIDE STREET — EVENING
Handheld macro at the counter: steam curling off a paper tray, chili oil bright red. She bites a dumpling in half, chews, dabs her mouth once with a thin napkin — and the napkin comes away clean. She raises an eyebrow at the lens.

Scene 6 — 5s
INT. SUBWAY PLATFORM — EVENING
Locked, eye-level. An express train slams past behind her, stainless steel doors strobing her reflection into a coral smear. Her hair lifts in the tunnel wind; she leans a fraction toward the moving steel, checking herself in a reflection too fast to hold, then laughs and gives up.

Scene 7 — 5s
INT. TRAIN CAR — CONTINUOUS
Handheld, tight, fluorescent light. Balanced on a lurching floor, she uncaps the tube one-handed, presses coral on by feel while the car sways, caps it, and drops it into her jacket pocket in one motion.

Scene 8 — 5s
EXT. CROSSTOWN CROSSWALK — NIGHT
Wide, handheld, taxis stacked and idling, office glass glowing behind. She jogs the crossing against the countdown, tote bouncing, and looks back over her shoulder at camera with a grin: "Made for the street."

Scene 9 — 5s
INT. CLUB BACK CORRIDOR — NIGHT
Handheld, low, brick and red exit-light spill. She pulls the tube from her pocket, gives it one dismissive glance, doesn't reapply, and shoves the curtain aside with her forearm as it lifts and swings.

Scene 10 — 6s
INT. COMEDY CLUB STAGE — NIGHT
Locked frame from the back of the room, hard single spotlight. She lifts the mic off the stand, leans into it, and the room's laughter breaks across her face — head tipping back, coral mouth wide open, shoulders shaking.

Scene 11 — 5s
INT. CLUB STAGE, TIGHT — CONTINUOUS
Push-in close on her face, punchy flash-lit contrast. Sweat at her temple, spotlight hot on her cheek, the coral still exactly where it started. She wipes her mouth with the flat of her hand, checks the hand, finds nothing, and smirks straight into the lens.

Scene 12 — 5s
INT. EMPTY STAGE, AFTER — NIGHT
Overhead flat-lay on the scuffed black stage floor, single work light: the coral tube lying beside the crumpled napkin set list and a sweating water bottle. Her hand reaches in, drags the tube toward her, closes around it, and lifts it out of frame.
